question: Why had the plane's velocity come apart from its nose at the torpedo release instant, and what commands the run-in speed and altitude?
answer: The velocity left the nose because the ONLY term that couples them was multiplied by zero. 007DBD3A/007DBD50 damp the body lateral velocity ctl+3Ch by desc+174h XDrag and the body vertical velocity ctl+40h by desc+170h YDrag, scaled by 007D92B0's response curve; nothing else in the native brings a rotated plane's velocity back onto its nose, because 0085E4D0 turns the pose and leaves the velocity where it is. PlaneFreeFlightClass declares x_drag and y_drag 0.0f and this host never filled them, so src/plane_flight.cpp:348-349 computed the right rule times zero. Fixed at the producer: the vehicle-class row reader now loads XDrag/YDrag/MaxSpd/TravelSpeed and the free-flight arm fills the class. The run-in SPEED is the spawn seed and nothing else: the host hard-coded 141.666672 m/s, which is the TravelSpeed of four rows in this installation, while both torpedo bombers author 61.111111 (220 km/h). There is no thrust or drag term in this host (PlaneFreeFlightState::thrust_accel and drag_accel are never set), so the commanded throttle cannot move a plane's speed even when it is published, and it is not published: r.commanded_throttle_2c8 is stored into a field nothing reads. Nothing commands an ALTITUDE at all - the aim tick's cmd+2BCh/cmd+2D0h outputs are dropped and command_altitude_and_throttle is an empty override - so the plane holds its 700 m spawn altitude. cmd+278h/+27Ch are NOT the altitude pair: 009D1F4A writes the constant 1.0 from 00D7A24C and 009D1F55 the byte 1.
coverage: complete for the body-damping block 007DBD37-007DBE0D and the throttle product 009D1BB8-009D1D39 read to cmd+2C8h; partial for the B fold's input slot [ESP+14h], which was taken by frame position and not traced through every PUSH/POP; desc+A4h, the altitude fold's knee, is unread.

contracts: desc+A4h, the altitude fold's knee, is unread and not in the plane class field table.
[ESP+14h], the B fold's input, is the time-to-target slot by frame position only.
PlaneFreeFlightState::thrust_accel and drag_accel (007D9050, unit+CC8h, 007D9140) are unmodelled, so no throttle command can change a plane's speed in this host.
The commanded altitude cmd+2BCh / cmd+2D0h is computed and dropped; command_altitude_and_throttle is an empty override.

validation.runner: tools/run_game.ps1, 3200 frames, --mission-frames 3000 at 0.05 s, both columns from this worktree; the before column is this branch with the three bindings switched off in a temporary compile-time constant that was removed before the commit, so both columns share one source tree and one census.
validation.attribution: USN02 is bit-identical in every printed figure and carries no aircraft at all (distance_moved 0.00 m, pose_rotations 0, thinks 0), so nothing in this packet can reach it; its 44 ship-tube swims are the no-regression evidence. In USN01 the velocity-to-nose angle goes from 84-91 degrees to 0.2 degrees and the worst airspeed from 688.59 m/s to 64.50 m/s, which also terminates the banked-plane spiral docs/PLANE_FREE_FLIGHT_PHYSICS.md left open: XDrag/YDrag were the missing damping. The one before-run drop was made by an aircraft at -14556 m doing 688 m/s and produced no torpedo damage in either column, so it is an artefact of that spiral rather than a lost capability. The 9.5 points of mission damage (229.5 to 220.0) is the strafing geometry moving with every plane's trajectory; no torpedo damage exists in either column.
validation.no_swim_next_gate: publish_pose has two call sites in src/game_hosts_units.cpp - unit creation and the ship body path - and the plane path never republishes. Every consumer of unit_pose, including the gunnery drop origin, sees each aircraft frozen at its spawn placement, which is what produced the '700 m' release altitude in a log whose own census read -14556 m at the same instant. No air-dropped round can leave from where the aircraft is until that call exists.
